# Detection Backlog

The techniques RASD exercises with an offensive test but does not detect yet, ranked for the next rules: first the gaps whose rule can be written and validated in the lab today (RASD maps the telemetry and the red test produces it), then those that need only a red test step, then those that need a new log source. Ties go to the number of tracked groups with a documented ATT&CK procedure for the technique. Tracked groups are the ones curated in [actors.yml](../mappings/actors.yml) for RASD's techniques; ATT&CK lists more for most of them. The actor rows for these techniques were checked against attack.mitre.org on 2026-10-13. Source: [backlog.yml](../mappings/backlog.yml).

## Procedures behind the rank

### T1083 · File and Directory Discovery

- **APT28** ([G0007](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0007/)): Forfiles to locate PDF, Excel and Word documents
- **Lazarus Group** ([G0032](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0032/)): Malware that finds files by extension and lists the files on every drive
- **HAFNIUM** ([G0125](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0125/)): Searched file contents on a compromised host
- **Fox Kitten** ([G0117](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0117/)): WizTree to list network files and directories
- **APT39** ([G0087](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0087/)): Tools that search for files on a compromised host

These are Windows file searches. The red test emulates Linux SUID and capability discovery, for which ATT&CK (T1548.001, Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid) names no group, only two malware families.

### T1505.003 · Server Software Component: Web Shell

- **OilRig** ([G0049](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049/)): Web shells to maintain access to victim networks
- **APT28** ([G0007](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0007/)): A modified, obfuscated reGeorg web shell for persistence
- **HAFNIUM** ([G0125](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0125/)): Several web shells on compromised servers, including SIMPLESEESHARP and SPORTSBALL
- **APT29** ([G0016](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0016/)): Web shells on exploited Microsoft Exchange servers
- **Fox Kitten** ([G0117](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0117/)): Web shells on compromised hosts to maintain access
- **APT39** ([G0087](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0087/)): ANTAK and ASPXSPY web shells
- **Volt Typhoon** ([G1017](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1017/)): Web shells including AuditReport.jspx and iisstart.aspx

### T1087.002 · Account Discovery: Domain Account

- **OilRig** ([G0049](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049/)): net user /domain and net group "domain admins" /domain to list domain accounts
- **MuddyWater** ([G0069](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0069/)): cmd.exe net user /domain to enumerate domain users
- **Wizard Spider** ([G0102](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0102/)): net group "Domain admins" /DOMAIN, and Get-ADComputer to collect account names
- **Fox Kitten** ([G0117](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0117/)): The Softerra LDAP browser to browse documentation on service accounts
- **Volt Typhoon** ([G1017](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1017/)): net group /dom and net group "Domain Admins" /dom for account discovery

### T1606 · Forge Web Credentials

- **APT29** ([G0016](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0016/)): In the SolarWinds compromise (C0024), SAML tokens forged with stolen signing certificates and an OWA cookie generated from a stolen key (T1606.002, T1606.001)

## How each gap gets validated

| Technique | Validation in the lab | Why there is no rule yet |
|---|---|---|
| T1083 | The red test already runs the three commands | Sysmon for Linux is mapped, but each of these commands is ordinary administration on its own. The signal is the set of them from one session in a short window, and that needs a baseline of Linux administration before it can alert without noise. |
| T1505.003 | The upload test does not run what it uploads; the rule needs a lab step in which the lab application starts a harmless command | The filename of an upload lives in the request body, which access logs do not record; only a WAF or the application sees it. |
| T1087.002 | A read-only `net group "Domain Admins" /domain` step in ldap_enumeration would produce the process event | No log source in the default Windows audit policy records LDAP query filters. Event 1644 needs verbose diagnostics on every DC, and 4662 only covers objects with a SACL. |
| T1606 | The red test already sends unsigned and tampered tokens; the application has to log the failures | Access logs normally do not record the Authorization header, so the forged token is invisible to a log-based rule unless the application logs validation failures. |
